title: Revenue tile shows Parts and Labor as whole percentages, or the invoice count
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a fresh test location made for this run, so nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  3. You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  4. A test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101). Its Default Shop Supplies is 0, so the invoice carries only labor and parts.
  5. An in-stock inventory part with a Sell price (e.g. $100.00) that this location can sell.
  6. Advisor A: you (Admin ShopView); the Service Advisor in the work order's left panel shows your name by default.
  7. One work order for that customer, ready but not invoiced yet: Service Advisor Advisor A, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour (Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00) with the part added (quantity 1, In stock); line completed and the work order marked reviewed.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: create a fresh location for every run (use a new name each time, for example ZZAUTOTEST Quiet plus today's date and a letter): profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name, Address 1, City, State/Province, ZIP/Postal Code, Timezone, Telephone, Shop Supplies Charge 0 > Save & Close. Switch to it: click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. While you are in it, add the labor rate this test uses (rates belong to each location): profile icon > Settings > Labor Rates > New Labor Rate: Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100, Rate 100) > Save & Close. Check: Dashboard > Revenue tile > range pill > This Week: it reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  • For 4: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save; on its Contacts tab: New Contact; add an asset (Add beside Asset in the New Work Order window, or the customer's Assets tab) and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field. Then on the customer page: edit icon > Edit Customer > Default Shop Supplies 0 > Save.
  • For 5: Parts > Inventory while in this location (pick a part with stock on hand, or use New Inventory Part).
  • For 6: the Service Advisor is in the work order's left panel; pick another name there for a second advisor.
  • For 7: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); set Service Advisor to Advisor A in the left panel; in the New Line window (> New Line on the Lines tab for each further line): What Are You Doing? ZZAUTOTEST Labor 2h, Add Technician (yourself), Labor Rate the $100 rate you added in this location (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100), Estimated Time 2 and Tech Time 2, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; on the line click Add Part, choose the inventory part, quantity 1, and make sure it shows In stock; on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed. Do not invoice yet.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Revenue tile's range pill to This Week and read the line under the amount.
  2. Click Work Orders, open the prepared work order, click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice. Close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying.
  3. On the invoice write down the labor total and the parts total (e.g. Labor $200.00 = 2.00 hours x $100.00, Parts $100.00). If the invoice also shows shop supplies, write that amount down too.
  4. Work out the split by hand: Parts = $100.00 / ($100.00 + $200.00) x 100 = 33.33, shown as 33. Labor = $200.00 / $300.00 x 100 = 66.67, shown as 67.
  5. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week again and read the line under the amount.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Before the invoice: Revenue reads $0.00 and the line under it reads "0 Invoices", because there is no parts-and-labor split to show.
  • After the invoice: the line reads "Parts 33% · Labor 67%", each a whole number (33.33 rounds to 33, 66.67 rounds to 67), and the two add up to 100.
  • If the invoice carried shop supplies and your percentages differ only because of them, mark the case Blocked and write all three amounts in the comment: the specification does not say which side shop supplies fall on.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S4 (S4-R3, S4-N2), S3 (S3-E3, Revenue split sentence). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After ("Parts 7% · Labor 93%"), 15_Empty_Design ("0 Invoices").

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%", each percent shown as a whole number.”
  • S4-N2: “If the Revenue tile has no parts-versus-labor split to show, its supporting line reads "{count} Invoices" instead.”
  • S3-E3 (Revenue split sentence): “The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
